questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were good, but not the largest selection

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine, a little higher than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UIB there could be more of showing up to classes, which I was used to in Copenhagen. There was only lectures and almost no time for discussing the lectures. More time at the courses could have been good, also for getting to know the other students better.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Climate policy
Environmental psychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both courses. But I liked the environmental psychology a lot, it was very interdisciplinary.

questions.answer: UiB friluft or being a member of an association

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you like hiking Bergen is a great place to visit, many different mountains surrounding Bergen. It also have some very good museums to visit, Bergen kunsthall.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Bergen and Copenhagen is quite similar, so it was easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People from Norway, a little like Denmark is not the greatest it being open to other people. But if you have classes with locals, just ask them for tips to see in the city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not so many cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the nature being so close to the city, and everyone going to the mountains when having time off and if the weather is good

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to join a social activity or association off your choice. 
Go hiking in the mountains around Bergen
If you like partying Fantoft is good, but else it is nice to live in the city close to the university and exploring the city by foot!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many nice places to visit in Bergen, both by bus and boat

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The many beautiful hikes, meeting new people and getting to know Bergen!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on your own in a new city was a little hard a first, but also a very great challenge!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
